title: Vertra product (product.yaml), format v2
description: One product: a container image and the actions it runs. Its image path is derived from its folder, catalog/<team>/<name>/, so it has no image field.

apiVersion.description: The catalog format: vertra.dev/v2. A file without it is from before v2: ./vertra catalog migrate rewrites it.

team.description: The team (team) folder this product is in.

version.description: Its contract's version, 1 when left out. Raise it for a breaking change (an action, input or output removed or retyped, a new required input, a team no longer shared with): vertra catalog check refuses one otherwise, since other teams' templates rely on the contract.

runtime.description: Documentation only: what the image runs on, such as python3.12.

serviceAccount.description: Optional. The Kubernetes ServiceAccount the product runs as, for a cloud identity bound to it. Without one, it runs as default.

tokenAudiences.description: Optional. Audiences its steps get a short-lived ServiceAccount token for, to sign in to another cloud by OIDC federation: sts.amazonaws.com (AWS), api://AzureADTokenExchange (Azure), or a GCP workload identity provider. Each is at /platform/tokens/<audience>, its characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._-] replaced by _. Never the cluster's own (the Kubernetes API's); the console refuses those.

errors.description: What the error codes your actions report mean, and what to do about each: shown on the run page when a step fails with one, beside whether retrying is safe (idempotent) and where to ask your team (team.yaml's help).

means.description: What happened, for the person whose run failed.

do.description: What they can do about it.

deprecated.description: Marks it deprecated, saying what to use instead. It keeps working; the console shows the message to everyone who uses it.

jsonSchemaObject.description: A JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) for an object.

script.description: Documentation only: where the action's code is.

secretRefs.description: The team secrets this action uses, each mounted at /platform/secrets/<name>/: its bindings, reviewed with the code that reads them. A team registers the secrets themselves (the console's Secrets tab); keys and description say what each must hold.

shareWith.description: The other teams that may run this action or include it in their templates, or ["*"] for every team. Left out, only its own team.

visibility.description: listed (the default): every team sees this action in the console, and those it isn't shared with can ask for access. hidden: only its own team sees it, so it can't have shareWith.

deprecated.description: Marks it deprecated, saying what to use instead. It keeps working; the console shows the message to everyone who uses it.

idempotent.description: Running it again with the same inputs does no harm: it finds what an earlier attempt made instead of making it twice. Required for maxAttempts above 1, so a step that failed on the platform's side (a reclaimed node, a lost Job, a timeout) is retried only when that's safe.

maxAttempts.description: How many times a step of this action may run in all before it fails: 1 (the default) means no retries. More than 1 needs idempotent: true. A template or DAG may ask for fewer, never more.

concurrencyKey.description: The inputs that name what a step of this action changes (a project, a database). While one step with the same values is starting or running, another waits its turn instead of changing the same thing at once. Values an earlier step produced count too.

approval.description: When a step of this action waits for a person to approve it before it runs: always, or otherTeams (only when another team runs it). A maintainer of this team approves or declines it on the run's page, never the person who ran it; nobody deciding within the install's approval timeout (3 days by default) fails it with APPROVAL_EXPIRED. Left out: never, unless a rule of your team.yaml's allowedTargets asks for one.
